question_options.question: How would you rate this pack?
How many tries did it take you to get the good ending?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Can you keep a secret?

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Sure!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I found this device attached to the camera in Principal Shapiro's office.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Principal Shapiro has a camera in her office? Because one time, Kat and I were in there, and we ended up... Well, uh, never mind. Why were you in Shapiro's office?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: The prom tiara's been stolen. I've been hired to track it down.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Whoa, the prom tiara? That thing's worth millions!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Yeah, I know. And I'm starting to think we might be dealing with someone savvier than your average thief.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: I never thought loaning something that expensive to the school was a good idea. It was driving the popular girls even crazier than usual!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Explain.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Taylor and Paula! The two of them are neck-and-neck in the running for prom queen, at least according to the newspaper polls, and they've been treating the thing like it's a World War!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Forcing people to take sides... Writing scathing editorials... Burning each other in effigy... It's ugly, Andy. Real ugly.
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Thanks for the tip, Brendan! That might come in handy.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Wow, this is so cool... Like a real detective novel! Can I be your plucky sidekick? Because I can do plucky...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: 'Elementary, my dear Brendan'... Kind of rolls off the tongue, doesn't it?

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: It totally does! Let me know if you need any more help!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Not this time, Brendan. I can't risk bringing you in on this one.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: What's wrong? You don't think I can handle myself? I beat up all those guys on the wrong side of town! I broke out of boot camp! I survived in the wild!

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Wow, I'm pretty awesome.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: It's not like that. This case is just too sensitive. We're talking high stakes, and I don't mean poker.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: You... You don't trust me? That's not right! I could totally make a good sidekick! I've got all kinds of intel!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Sorry, Brendan. You're on a need-to-know basis... And you don't need to know.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Yeah, well, you know what? This whole 'talking like a guy from an old movie' thing is really lame! So there!
Cold words, but these were cold times. I did what I had to do. The case was too important.
Still, as I walked away... I couldn't help but think that maybe Brendan could have helped me after all.
I'd gotten everything I could out of the cheerleaders. There was only one thing left to do... Scope out the scene of the crime.
The Principal's office was just like Paula had described it...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Let's see here... The window is broken, leaving shattered glass all over the parking lot outside...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: The display case has been forced open... And there's a big gaping hole where the tiara should be!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Time for some good old-fashioned detective work! There's got to be some hidden clues around here!
I walked over to the display case and examined it closely. I could see the scuff marks on the door where someone had pried it open...
And that was when I saw it. Wedged into the carpet just under the case was a single broken-off fake fingernail. Color: bright pink.
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Jackpot!
The person who broke into this case was either a girl or a guy with some interesting fashion choices. Either way, I had a solid clue.
I walked over to the display case and checked it out carefully...
But I couldn't find anything. Whoever hit this place had covered their trail perfectly!
That, or maybe I just didn't do a very good job looking for clues. What can I say? I was tired, and I had an Honors Pre-Calc mid-term that day!
I turned to walk outside... When I heard a distinct buzzing noise coming from a large statue of Lyle the Lizard.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: No way... It can't be...
But of course, it was. Shapiro had a hidden camera in her office, built into the lizard statue. She always was sharp as a switchblade.
Well, this wasn't the most exciting way to end a case, but a suspect's a suspect. I lifted the statue, reached inside to check out the tape...
And that was when I noticed the jamming device on the side of the camera.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You've got to be kidding me!
The device was fancy, nicer than any I'd ever seen. For the first time, I wondered just how deep this rabbit hole went... And what was waiting for me at the bottom.
I quickly pocketed the device. For better or worse, I was in this till the end.
I knew a fellow who was handy when it came to tech. He seemed like a good guy, and it didn't hurt that he owed me a favor.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Look, Andy, I really don't have much time... I've got to get this week's issue of The Centerscore Herald to print...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I know, I know. You're a busy man. Just take a quick look at this.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Whoa! Is that... A video interceptor?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That's my best guess.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Let's see... It takes a loop of footage... And uses it to tape over everything else!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: So if I had a loop of, say, an empty office...

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Then that's all that the camera would ever tape, even if people were coming in and out!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Sounds like pretty sophisticated tech. You know anyone at this school that would be able to make something like this?

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Oh no, no way... The engineering on this is `way` too sophisticated. The only person I can think of that would even come close is that nerd girl at Wilson... Steph.
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh no, no way... The engineering on this is [color=#e23b3b][i]way[/i][/color] too sophisticated. The only person I can think of that would even come close is that nerd girl at Wilson... Steph.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Thanks for the tip, Brendan. I'll go check it out.

nodes.speaker: Brendan
nodes.text: Wait a minute! Aren't you going to tell me what this is all about?
I thought about it, and decided...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Hey, Taylor! Can I get a minute of your time?

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: Uh, sure. Amanda, you wait right here and hold my pom-poms!

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Hee hee! Pom-poms!
Taylor and I wandered over to the edge of the bleachers.

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: What's the deal, freakshow? Looking for a prom date? Because I am `way` out of your league!
nodes.text_bbcode: What's the deal, freakshow? Looking for a prom date? Because I am [color=#3b78e2][i]way[/i][/color] out of your league!

nodes.text: Taylor hated me ever since I broke her leg during the whole Homecoming debacle. Guess some people carry a grudge.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You wouldn't even know where my league began, sugar. And what I want is to ask you a couple of questions.

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: Um, okay...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Do you remember anything unusual happening last night at cheerleading practice?

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: What, you mean besides Paula doing her usual crazy dictator routine and working us `way` too hard? Jessica passed out from dehydration... Again!
nodes.text_bbcode: What, you mean besides Paula doing her usual crazy dictator routine and working us [color=#3b78e2][i]way[/i][/color] too hard? Jessica passed out from dehydration... Again!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Crazy dictator... Sounds like Paula all right.

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: The worst part is, she's a total hypocrite! She missed three practices this month to hang out with that stupid mystery boyfriend of hers!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Mystery boyfriend?

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: Ugh, yeah, we all know she's dating some new guy, but she totally won't tell us who he is!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You're sure about this?

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: Totally! The other day, I was eavesdropping on her phone conversation, and she was calling some guy 'honey', 'cutey', and 'sugarbuns'!
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Interesting. Very interesting.

nodes.speaker: Taylor
nodes.text: Why do you care, anyway? Planning to ask her to prom?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You've got a singularly one-track mind, Taylor. Stay out of trouble.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Hey, Amanda! Can I ask you a couple of questions?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Sure! Just no fractions, okay? I hate fractions...
Amanda and I wandered over to the edge of the bleachers.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: What's up?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Do you recall anything out of the ordinary happening last night during cheerleading practice?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Last night... Last night... What was last night, again? Thursday or Friday?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: It was Monday.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Monday? But I thought Monday was last week!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Right. Look, let's try this again. Do you know anything about the prom tiara?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: It's sparkly!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That's it? That's all you've got?

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: Well, it `is!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, it [color=#3b78e2][i]is![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Okay, well, that's a wrap. Take care of yourself, sweetheart.
The girl had a great heart, but she was as a bright as a plate of sauerkraut. Talking to her was a dead end.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: It's the prom queen tiara! It's been stolen!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That flimsy, plastic crown you wore last year? Why would anyone care about that?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Okay, first of all, never, `ever` denigrate the timeless symbol of social power that is the prom queen tiara!
nodes.text_bbcode: Okay, first of all, never, [color=#3b78e2][i]ever[/i][/color] denigrate the timeless symbol of social power that is the prom queen tiara!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: And second of all, don't you know anything? The plastic crown is `out!` A few weeks ago, Silas Prince donated his great-grandmother's diamond-encrusted tiara for us to use at prom!
nodes.text_bbcode: And second of all, don't you know anything? The plastic crown is [color=#3b78e2][i]out![/i][/color] A few weeks ago, Silas Prince donated his great-grandmother's diamond-encrusted tiara for us to use at prom!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: This thing is way, way nice. I mean, really, just like gorgeous!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Sounds pricey. If this thing's stolen, why isn't the school crawling with cops?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Because no one knows it's missing but me!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: My interest is officially piqued. Spill the beans.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Last night, I was at school late for cheerleading practice... There's a big game coming up, and with Trippy-Toes Taylor on our team, we've got a `lot` of practicing to do!
nodes.text_bbcode: Last night, I was at school late for cheerleading practice... There's a big game coming up, and with Trippy-Toes Taylor on our team, we've got a [color=#3b78e2][i]lot[/i][/color] of practicing to do!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I stepped out to the lockers to get a drink of my Diet Protein Water, when I heard a terrible crash from inside Principal Shapiro's office!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: By the time I got there, it was too late... Shapiro's display case was broken open, and the tiara was gone!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Did you see anything else?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: The window was shattered, and for just one second, I thought I saw someone running away across the parking lot...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: And no one else knows about this?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Shapiro's out of town for a Singles Retreat or whatever, but she comes back tomorrow morning! You need to find the crown and get it back before she knows it's gone!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Why is this so important to you, anyway? Why not just let the fuzz handle it?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Uh, hello? Borrowing this tiara was a huge honor for the school... And a huge liability!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Principal Shapiro told the Spirit Committee that if anything happened to it, she'd cancel prom! The most important social event of the year!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I'm a senior, Andy. If I graduate high school without getting to attend my senior prom, I might as well just check myself into the Shady Creek Retirement Home, because my life is `over!`
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm a senior, Andy. If I graduate high school without getting to attend my senior prom, I might as well just check myself into the Shady Creek Retirement Home, because my life is [color=#3b78e2][i]over![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: All right, I think I've got the high and low of it. I'll take your case, Paula... But that doesn't mean anything's changed between us!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: You won't regret helping me, Andy, I promise... Now find that tiara!
I had to admit, I was excited. A high stakes prize, a shady dame, and a ticking clock... Now `this` was the kind of case I could sink my teeth into!
nodes.text_bbcode: I had to admit, I was excited. A high stakes prize, a shady dame, and a ticking clock... Now [b]this[/b] was the kind of case I could sink my teeth into!

nodes.text: My first stop was the football field. The cheerleaders and I weren't on the greatest terms, not since I exposed their annual car wash as a glorified Ponzi scheme, but they were still my best lead.
If the crime happened during cheerleading practice, maybe one of the other girls had heard something. The question was, which one should I put the screws to?

nodes.prompt: Which one should I put the screws to?

menu.title: Make your choice!
menu.text: Which one should I put the screws to?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I don't even want to know what you're mixed up in, Paula. You're nothing but trouble, and I've already got enough trouble for a family of four.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Look, I was being nice by asking for your help, Andy. The truth is, you don't have a choice.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: What's that supposed to mean?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Oh, nothing much. I just wonder what Principal Shapiro would say if she knew about the slingshot in your locker...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That's for self-defense!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Oh really? And what about the fireworks, the ninja weapons, and the copy of 'Wiretapping for Dummies'?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: How do you know all this?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: My dad's one of the richest men in Centerscore, Andy. I have a way of finding things out.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Then why exactly do you need my help?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I said richest, Andy. I didn't say smartest. Now are you going to take my case, or do I need to have a talk with Principal Shapiro?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: So that's how it's going to be, huh? You're blackmailing me?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: It's working, isn't it?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I guess it is.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Great! I'm sooooo glad we're on the same page.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Let's just get this over with. What exactly do you want me to track down?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I'll hear you out, but I'm not promising anything. I don't work pro bono.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: What does an overrated rock star have to do with anything?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I mean, I don't work for free.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Oh, you don't have to worry about that. Help me out, and I'll make sure you're handsomely rewarded. You `know` I'm good for it... My dad's one of the richest men in town!
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh, you don't have to worry about that. Help me out, and I'll make sure you're handsomely rewarded. You [color=#3b78e2][i]know[/i][/color] I'm good for it... My dad's one of the richest men in town!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Well, I suppose I could use a little spare cheddar... I did see that stylish designer eye patch in 'Facial Accessories Weekly'...

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I'm glad we're on the same page. I knew I could count on you!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Yeah, yeah. Now what exactly do you want me to track down?
By the time I got back to Centerscore, night had fallen, and I was no closer to an answer.
I hated to admit defeat, but Paula was my client, and I had to let her know I hadn't found the tiara. I drove up to her mansion and let myself in through her window.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Paula.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Eep! Andy! What are you doing sneaking in my window, you creeper?!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I had to talk to you. I've got some bad news.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Ugh, let me guess. You didn't find the tiara, did you?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I'm afraid not. The evidence, it... It's not adding up.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Well, listen, you might be in luck. I was just lying in bed filing my nails when I remembered something else about last night!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Oh?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Yeah! Remember how I thought I saw someone running from Shapiro's office? I'm pretty sure they had blond hair!

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: And I think he... Or maybe she... Was wearing some kind of uniform!
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Blonde... Uniform... Interesting. Very, very interesting.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Uh, no, what's interesting is you finding out who stole the stupid thing! Now get out there and do your job!
I turned around to go back the way I came in... And that was when I heard `it.`
nodes.text_bbcode: I turned around to go back the way I came in... And that was when I heard [b]it.[/b]

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Paula... Are you alone in your house?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: I... I am... Why?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Because I'm pretty sure I just heard someone sneaking around in your living room!
I shoved Paula aside and sprinted into the living room... Just in time to see a shifty figure rush out the door!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: What the... Someone's spying on me! We've got us a peeping Tom!
I ran into the street and nearly got run down by a car frantically peeling out. I sprinted to my car...
And took off in hot pursuit!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: So you think you can tail me, punk?! Who are you?! What are you after?!
My heart was racing faster than a souped-up Lamborguinnea. There was no way I was letting that car get away!
I floored it! The two of us raced down the streets like a couple of arrows fired blindly into the darkness by some deranged Eastern-European woodsman.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Almost got ya... Almost got ya...
The other driver was no match for me. I put the pedal to the metal, raced up right alongside the car, and turned to get a good look...
And right then, the other car took a turn too hard, spun out of control, and went flying down a steep hill into the woods!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Well, that's not good.
By the time I parked and got down into the woods, the car was already abandoned, and the other driver was long gone.
It didn't matter though, because one look at the car's custom license plate gave me everything I needed...
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: 'T-PRINCE'. A literal peeping Tom. Fascinating.
I raced after the car, channeling every ounce of my fastness and ferocity...
It's just too bad I wasn't a very good driver.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Aiiiiiieeeeeeeeeeee!
Three hours later, after the tow truck fished my car out of the creek...

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: I'm very disappointed in you, son, very disappointed! What were you thinking driving like that? That's just plain reckless!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I'm sorry, Officer.

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: And I had such high expectations for you too! You were my favorite kid in town! I was going to make you my negligee!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I really hope you mean protege...

nodes.speaker: Officer Monte
nodes.text: And I really hope you mean 'I'm a huge, stupid failure who can't even drive straight!' Now get out of my sight before I write you out of my will!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Fine. You've made your point. I'll show myself out. If you decide you want to help me find this tiara, you know my number.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: I'm not joking, Andy! This case is dangerous! You need to get out while you can.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Typical Lucretia. Always worrying that I'm in too much danger, convinced that I'm in over my head.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: That's because you always `are` in over your head! I know you love this whole private eye act you've got going on, but there are bad people out there, people you don't want to cross!
nodes.text_bbcode: That's because you always [color=#3b78e2][i]are[/i][/color] in over your head! I know you love this whole private eye act you've got going on, but there are bad people out there, people you don't want to cross!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: What's the worst they could do? Tell me they loved me and then break up with me a week later? Because I'll tell you, angel, someone beat them to it.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Ugh! There's just no getting through to you! Get out of here then, and take your stupid 1940's voice with you! Go! `Go!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Ugh! There's just no getting through to you! Get out of here then, and take your stupid 1940's voice with you! Go! [color=#3b78e2][i]Go![/i][/color]

nodes.text: I got out of there faster than a cheerleader at a sci-fi convention.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Stupid, arrogant, know-it-all, no-good jerk!

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: ...Be careful.
It was a long walk back to my car. Every step I took, I wondered if I'd made a mistake... But there was no room in my life for turning back. Not anymore.
She jerked away, just for a second... And then she leaned right back into the kiss. She tasted like sunlight, and I held her for as long as I possibly could.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: That... That wasn't fair.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Whoever said anything about love being fair?

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: You... You've got to get out of here. It'll be night soon. You know what happens at night.
I thought of his pale, twisted skin... Those hollow, empty eyes... That voice, like dust blowing out of a tomb...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: All right. I won't waste any more of your time.
I started to turn... When she stepped up real close and whispered in my ear...

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: You're just a pawn in someone's game, Andy Canneloni. Just a pawn.
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Just... A pawn?
Then she kissed my cheek, just once, and turned away.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Take care of yourself, Andy.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You too, angel. You too.
Of course... Things never work out the way you want them to.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Yo! Cyclops! Get ready for a beat-down!
Travis Turducken. Tough as a gorilla and half as smart. Someone must have sent him after me... But who?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: You stuck your nose in the wrong case, buddy... And you're about to have it punched in!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That's ambiguous.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: What?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Your phrasing. It's ambiguous. What am I going to have punched in... My nose or my case? You've got an dangling modifier.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Shut up! I'll dangle your modifier!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Well now you're just being obscene.
Travis swung a right hook, and I dodged it effortlessly.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: It doesn't have to go down like this, Travis. You can still walk away.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Heh, you really think you can take me? How you gonna do that with no depth perception, freak?!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: On second thought, it `does` have to go down like this. You're going down, unibrow.
nodes.text_bbcode: On second thought, it [color=#e23b3b][i]does[/i][/color] have to go down like this. You're going down, unibrow.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Let's do this!
I thought I could beat him. I was faster, smarter, and trained in seventeen and a half martial arts.
But none of that made me feel any better when Travis planted his fist right in my gut.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Ooooof! Stop! No more! Please!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Had enough, eh? Ready to drop your case? Or do I have to beat some more common sense into you?
He was relaxing, lowering his guard, and underestimating how much fight I had left.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I... I promise... Just don't hit me any more...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Man, you're just pathetic! And here I thought you might at least put up a good fight...
I balled up my hand into a fist... Got ready for the swing... Waited for him to turn around...
And that was when Ryan ran up behind me and nailed me over the head with his skateboard.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You're making... A mistake... Ugh...
I hit the pavement, hard, and the lights went out.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Dude! You're supposed to be my driver! What are you doing?!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: He was winding up for a sucker-punch! I just saved your butt!
Fighting, when it comes right down to it, is just physics. Apply the right amount of force in the right location...
Say, a nice, powerful jab right in your opponent's solar plexus...
And you'll get precisely the reaction you want.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Stop! Please! No more! That really hurt!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Who hired you?! Who wants me off this case?

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: I don't know!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That's not good enough!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: No, please! Don't hit me again! I got a text message, okay? It said that if I came here and beat you up, I'd get paid two hundred dollars!
Clue Acquired!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: That's an awful lot of shekels just to see me beat up. Whoever did this must have some pretty deep pockets...
I was about to pry the goon for more intel...
And that was when Ryan ran up behind me and nailed me over the head with his skateboard.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Not... Fair... Sneak... Attack...
I hit the pavement, hard, and the lights went out.

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: Dude! You were supposed to wait in the car! What the heck?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: He was totally whooping you! I saved your butt!
Darkness washed over me like an ice-cold bath.
Somewhere far, far away, two voices were bickering...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: You knocked him out cold!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: I had no choice!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: What are we supposed to do with him now?

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: Heh, I know! We should take him and drop him on the wrong side of town!

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: We're already on the wrong side of town, you idiot! Just load him into the car, and we'll figure... Hey! Who's that? Get away from here!
I heard footsteps racing towards me, then the sounds of a scuffle... Then I couldn't hold out any longer, and all I knew was silence.
I woke up two hours later.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Huh... Where am... Uh oh.
I smelled old gasoline and rusted metal. I was in the abandoned car factory on the very edge of town... And that meant `she` was around.
nodes.text_bbcode: I smelled old gasoline and rusted metal. I was in the abandoned car factory on the very edge of town... And that meant [b]she[/b] was around.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Looking for me?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Aaaah! Lucretia! You startled me!

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Which makes me the second person to get the drop on you today. You're getting rusty in your old age!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Yeah, well... I've got a lot on my mind, okay?
Lucretia... The one that got away. She was as brilliant as she was beautiful, and twice as dangerous to boot. I'd loved her once... But that was a lifetime ago.
Well... Technically... Three months.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Thanks for the assist, I guess. I take it you took care of Goofus and Goliath?

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: I gave 'em a couple of bruises and sent them on their way. I doubt they'll be messing with you any time soon.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I appreciate that, but I really need to get going...

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Listen, Andy. I know why you're here on the Wilson side of town. I know all about your case.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Know who did it?

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: I know you're way out of your league. This isn't some petty theft or vandalized car. There are bigger forces at work here, bigger than you can imagine.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: Drop the case, Andy. Drop it before you get hurt.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: You don't get to tell me what to do. Not anymore. You lost that right when you broke up with me.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: You know it's not like that! I felt something for you that I've never felt for anyone else... But you know what I'm going through. You know what I have to deal with.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: I can't have anyone else in my life, not now, and if we kept seeing each other, then you'd be in too much danger! You know what `he'd` do to you!
nodes.text_bbcode: I can't have anyone else in my life, not now, and if we kept seeing each other, then you'd be in too much danger! You know what [color=#3b78e2][i]he'd[/i][/color] do to you!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I'm not afraid of your father, Lucretia.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: You should be, Andy. You should be.
I tried to look tough, but my gaze darted across the room to a huge steel door. It was still daytime, so he was still sleeping... I hoped.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I know the risk. I know what you're afraid of. But I would risk a thousand times more than that just to be with you. You know that.

nodes.speaker: Lucretia
nodes.text: And you know I just can't take that chance.
In that second, she looked more beautiful than ever. I felt like my heart was going to explode, and then I...

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Huh? Who are you? Is this about the Swiss bank accounts? Because I swear, I don't know how all that money got transferred...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Keep playing cute, freckles. That kind of talk will put you straight on the Juvey Express.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: If you want to keep that pretty little laptop of yours, you'll start answering questions, fast. Did you build this video interceptor? Why'd you build it? Who'd you build it for?!

nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Look, I don't know who you think you are or who you thought you were impressing with your gruff voice and your big threats and your fake eye patch...

nodes.speaker: Andy

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: But it's not going to work on me. The minute you sat down, my webcam started recording every second of this dumb, little act of yours.

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: So unless you want to beat out 'Krazy Kats' and 'Lightsword Boy' for the number one slot on YooTube, you'll turn around, walk out that door, and never talk to me again.

nodes.text: Are we clear?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Excuse me? Are you Stephanie Cha?

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Who wants to know?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I'm Mr. McGraw, the admissions officer at the Centerscore Academy of Technology. My focus? Scholarships.

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Oh! Well, uh, hi! Nice to meet you! You're a little bit young, aren't you?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: I've got a medical condition. That's one strike against you right there.

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Oh no!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Now then, what I wanted to talk to you about was your engineering skills. Specifically, this video interceptor that was found at Centerscore High. Do you know anything about it?

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Uh... Well... I mean...

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Now, now, don't worry about getting in trouble. At C.A.T., we don't worry about pedestrian things like human morality or basic decency. All that matters is the advancement of technology.

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: That's what I've been saying all along! Okay, yeah, I totally built that interceptor!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: It's a fascinating gadget, among the best I've ever seen. Can you tell me what inspired you to make it?

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Well, it's a funny story. I got this message over FaceSpace offering to pay me for it... I figured, what the heck, why not? A job's a job, right?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Any idea who this message was from?

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: No clue. The person had an anonymous account. The only thing I could deduce was that they were in the Centerscore High network.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Fascinating! That'll be all! Thanks for your time!

nodes.speaker: Steph
nodes.text: Wait! Don't you want to know about all my other technical qualifications? I made a computer that's capable of love!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Oh, I'm sure one of my colleagues will track you down sooner or later. Have a nice life!
So, the person who disabled the camera went to Centerscore. An inside job. A traitor. A turncoat. But why? I had to get back to Centerscore to find out.
After I left Brendan, I knew I had to go to Wilson High to check on this Steph girl.
I hadn't planned on coming back here... Not since that dark day... The day `she` said we couldn't see each other any more...

args.text: `WHAT?! How dare you?`
Andy, this is a very serious accusation! Explain yourself!
The case didn't make sense to me... Not until just now. All along, I thought this was about a stolen tiara... But what if the tiara was never the point?
Everyone knows Paula has hated Taylor since she got crowned Winter Queen. The two have been bitterly fighting for popularity... And lately, Taylor's been winning.

You said it yourself, Paula. Prom is the most important social event of the year. If Taylor was crowned prom queen, she'd be the most popular girl for sure... And you'd never have a chance to win it back.
Then again... How can you have a prom queen... Without a prom?
You knew Shapiro would cancel prom if the tiara went missing! That's why you stole it! This way, Taylor would never have a chance to really, truly beat you!
This is slander!
Oh, I'm just getting started, sweetheart.
Cheerleading practice provided the perfect cover. You snuck off to get some water, and then broke into the office!
You knew Shapiro had a camera, so you paid Steph to make you an interceptor...
And then, just to make it look like a robbery, you broke open the window. Of course, you broke it open from the inside... And that's why most of the glass was outside!
It was a win-win situation for you, Paula. Prom got cancelled, meaning that Taylor never got to be Queen... And you got to keep a beautiful piece of jewelry!
How did you describe it again? 'Really, just like, gorgeous'?
What happened next? Did you start to panic and worry that it might lead back to you? Or did you just decide to kill a third bird with that stone?
You'd heard my reputation. You knew that if anyone was going to trace this to you, it'd be me... So you hired me yourself to divert my suspicions!
And you gave me just enough clues to throw me off the trail. You saw someone running away... Someone blonde... And wearing a uniform?
You practically gave me a picture of Taylor! You wanted me to think it was her! Even if I couldn't prove it, the accusation alone would destroy her reputation!
Secure your popularity... Get a brand-new tiara... And destroy your biggest rival? Well, folks, that's what I call the perfect crime.
You can't prove any of this!
A cheerleading uniform is pretty snug, and you got yours cut extra-short. Not a lot of places to hide a tiara, and I bet you weren't bold enough to sneak it out during school hours.
You want proof, Principal Shapiro? Go check Paula's locker. You'll find the tiara there.
No! Don't! Don't do that!
Why on earth not?
Because I... Because it... I... I... Because... Because...
Fine! It was me! I did it, okay? I just... It's my senior year! My only one, ever! I couldn't let Taylor win prom queen! I couldn't!
Oh, Paula. I knew you had your problems... But I never, ever thought you'd do something like this...
Just one thing I don't understand. If I was doing your work all along... Why'd you hire Travis to intimidate me?
That wasn't me. That was my boyfriend. He thought I never should've tried to use you... He knew it would backfire! He just wanted to protect me!
Your boyfriend...
Tom Prince.
And then it hit me. The last piece of the puzzle... The one that made the picture clear.
Paula was the sticky red hand that had stolen the tiara... But Tom Prince was the brain.
All this time, I had failed to ask the most obvious, basic question... Why the heck would Silas Prince lend his tiara to Centerscore in the first place?!
He wouldn't... Not unless he had some master plan!
Now son, you know what you have to do...
I won't let you down!
Tom started dating Paula... Sweet-talked her... And then he put the idea in her head.
I mean, this is your Senior Prom! If Taylor wins prom queen, you'll regret it for the rest of your life!
But what am I supposed to do?
Well... I have an idea...
Tom Prince was the person lurking around Paula's house... But he hadn't been stalking me.
He'd just been visiting his girlfriend!
Of course, knowing Tom, there was absolutely no proof of his involvement. He'd get off scot-free... And Paula would take the fall.
You wait here, Paula. I... I have to go call the police. This is a very serious situation. Very serious.
I'm so disappointed in you.
The old bird fluttered off. Paula slumped to her knees and started to cry.
Sniffle... Sniffle... My life... Is over!
It's not that bad, sweetheart. There's always college, right?
I went over to the Wilson side of town that afternoon. I hadn't planned on it... But there was someone I had to see.
I heard you cracked your case.
I did, but I don't feel good about it. I figured out the who and the how, but I just can't figure out the why.
Why would Silas Prince set Paula up like that? What does he have to gain? What is his master plan?
She stepped forward and pressed her hand to the side of my face.
Forget it, Andy. It's Centerscore.
Meanwhile, in Silas Prince's office, Silas is having a meeting... With Paula's dad!
My, my, my, These are some very serious charges! And what's worse, your daughter is eighteen... That means she'll be tried as an adult!
If my knowledge of the justice system is correct, I think she'll be looking at 10 years in prison, minimum!
No! Please! Don't do that to my baby girl! She's all I have!
Well, I might be willing to drop the charges if you'll just do me one little favor...
I'll do anything! Anything!
Sign over your assets to me! I want all of them... Your land... Your business... Your four houses... `Everything!`
Silas slams some papers on the table and hands Paula's dad a pen. Paula's dad tearfully takes the pen, sniffles, and signs them.
Pleasure doing business with you, Fred!
You're a monster, Silas! A monster! And some day, someone's gonna give you exactly what you deserve!
Yeah, yeah, blah blah. Security! Come immediately! There appears to be a beggar in my office!
You cracked the case, got back the tiara, and maybe even helped Andy work something out with Lucretia! Congrats!
What's that Silas Prince up to, though? What's his master plan?
You'll just have to play another episode and find out!
Imagine watching a mystery where the detective almost solves the crime but doesn't quite get it. That would be pretty lame, huh? So is `almost` playing a perfect game!

You played a perfect game! Way to go, gumshoe! Enjoy your bonus scene!
Andy's got a pretty odd way of seeing the world... But he's not the only one!
Captain's Log... Stardate 2010. Grizzled space-marine Dexter X Ironface snuck sneakily along the hallways of the Centerscore space station...
It was quiet, he thought, too quiet... Or maybe not quiet enough. Also possibly just the right amount of quiet. That was another option.
But Dexter X Steeljaw had no time for concerns like that! He was on a mission of the utmost galactic importance!
The beautiful Space Princess Ashley was in the station's library, going over planetary trade agreements, and he'd volunteered to help her study!
You see, it turns out Dexter X Copperbreath was not just the universe's toughest, coolest, most wise-crackiest space marine, but he was also pretty good at history... Er... Trade agreements.
Hey you! Nerd-who-isn't-Spud! I just got my butt kicked by some crazy pirate ninja girl, and I need to vent some frustration!
Just stand still and let me hit you a couple of times, okay? Don't make this any harder than it has to be...
Travis the Terminator. The world's deadliest cyborg, more machine than man. I'd had my run-ins with him before... But this time I was ready.
Back away, android... Or prepare to be disintegrated!
Is that... A water gun? You're threatening me with a water gun? Really? That's the best you can do?
You were given fair warning! Now die, brigand!
Dexter blasts Travis in the face... And Travis stumbles back, screaming!
Aaaaaaaahhhhh! What is this?! Hot sauce?! It's in my eyes! It burnnnnnnnns!
Call a nurse! Call a doctor! Call the President!
Sorry, cyborg. If you can't handle the heat... Get out of the galaxy!
That doesn't... Even... Make... Sense...
A foe vanquished, a super-weapon deployed, and the galaxy safe yet again. Just another day in the life of Dexter X Razorpants... Space Marine!
Hope you enjoyed that little peek into Dexter's mind! See you in another episode!

I thought closely about all the evidence I'd gotten...
The window was shattered, and for just one second, I thought I saw someone running away across the parking lot...
She missed three practices this month to hang out with that stupid mystery boyfriend of hers!

And then it hit me, like a breath of fresh air blown out of an industrial strength fan. Suddenly, I knew the truth.

Taylor knew where it was kept, and she knew she'd be at school late for cheerleading practice.
So while everyone was busy, she broke into your office and stole it!
She had everything covered. She even hired Steph to make her a video interceptor to take care of your security camera...
But the one thing she didn't count on was Paula seeing her running away... And getting a good look at her blonde hair and her cheerleading uniform!
She was willing to ruin prom for everyone... Just to keep the tiara?! She's a monster! I always knew she had it in her!
You're sure of this, Andy? You're positive?
%s had to be guilty. I was 100 percent certain...
And I was 100 percent wrong.
The fuzz searched %s's house, and didn't find a trace.
Even worse, my 100 percent certain suspect turned out to have a 100 percent perfect alibi.
We reviewed Amanda's cell phone, and the photos on the camera show that she was at cheerleading practice all night!
I `know` she was at practice! I'm saying she snuck off!
I don't think you understand. According to our forensics team, that girl takes a photo of herself roughly every eleven seconds. And all of them show her at practice!
Her alibi checks out, son. She's innocent.
I just don't get it... I was so sure... I've never been this wrong...
Look, cupcake, let's drop the facade. I checked out your little theory to be nice... But we all know you did it!
What? What are you talking about?
I had my boys do a full sweep of Shapiro's office. Guess what they found? Your sticky little fingerprints all over her surveillance camera!
Oh, right... I probably should've cleaned those up...
Uh! I mean... What fingerprints?
Spare me the innocent act, son. I've seen this story a thousand times before... Good cop gets too close to a crime, gets greedy, goes crooked. Nothing new under the sun.
Listen, Officer, you and I go way back. You `know` me!

Don't you worry, son. You're not going to Juvey. I'll see to it you get sent somewhere a whole lot better than that...
I think I know where this is going...
Welcome to Officer Monte's Boot Camp for Troubled Youth! And boy, do I have a great regimen planned out for you!
Falsely accused. Wrongfully imprisoned. Trapped behind bars. I'd been in worse situations... But not by much.
There was only one thing I could do... Escape!
Oh, and don't even think about escaping! Since our last little breakout incident, I've installed state-of-the-art security measures!
Electrified fences! Motion detectors! An entire army of trained badgers!
No one ever said it'd be easy... But that didn't mean I wasn't going to try.

Can... Can you hear my voice-over?
Childhood exposure to a staggering quantity of radioactive paint chips has gifted me with powerful telepathic abilities! How do you think I'm such a good cop?
Now get to work, son! That freshwater canal isn't going to desalinate itself!

I'm sorry, sugar, what can I say? Sometimes you beat the case, sometimes the case beats you!
Yeah, well, guess what? Everyone is royally ticked! Principal Shapiro is cancelling prom!
I gave you one simple job, and you ruined everything! I swear on my designer Luis Briton purse... I will destroy you, Andy Cannelloni. Consider yourself socially dead!
Hmph!
Okay, so prom's cancelled. So the whole school will probably hate me. Fine. I'll get over it. What's the worst that could happen?
When Silas Prince found out the tiara was gone, he was more than royally ticked. He was so mad, he pulled some strings with his cronies on the Accreditation Board.
That meant Centerscore got shut down, and `that` meant we all had to go to Wilson!
Okay, okay. So I'm stuck in a new high school full of people that totally hate me...
And okay, so I have to walk home at night across the Wilson side of town. Fine. What's the worst that could happen?
dooooooooom...
Huh? Where did that come from? I'm not scared of you! I know you can't hurt me!
Show yourself! Come out and fight me like a man!
i am... not... a man!
Aaaaaaaaaaiiiiiieeeeeeeee!
Okay, so I got dragged off into the shadows by a terrifying, possibly-undead ghoul. What's the worst that could happen?
Hmm. Don't answer that.
This may just be the worst ending we've ever had. Sure, Andy's kind of weird, but he doesn't deserve... That!

nodes.text: Darkness washed over me like an ice-cold bath.
Somewhere far, far away, two voices were bickering...

nodes.speaker: Travis
nodes.text: You knocked him out cold!

nodes.speaker: Ryan
nodes.text: I had no choice!
As the world faded away, I wondered how I'd gotten myself into this mess... But let's start from the beginning.
See that fellow there with the dapper eye patch and the devil-may-care attitude?
That's me, Andy Cannelloni, and I'm the closest thing this town has to a private eye.

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: So you see, Officer Monte, the person who kidnapped the mayor's Chihuahua is `clearly` Mr. Pibb!
nodes.text_bbcode: So you see, Officer Monte, the person who kidnapped the mayor's Chihuahua is [color=#e23b3b][i]clearly[/i][/color] Mr. Pibb!

nodes.text: Six months ago, this was a great little town... Clean streets, nice shops, well-behaved citizens...
But lately, things had changed. Life had gotten rough, ugly, and lean. Everywhere I looked, I saw shuttered windows, bankrupt businesses, and foreclosed homes.
Lean times meant desperate people. And desperate people... Meant trouble.
It all started this morning. I was walking to class when I heard the deadliest, cruelest, most powerful sound in the world...
A dame in trouble.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Andy! Andy! I need to talk to you!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Save it, sugar. My life's only got room for one needy harpy, and I've already got a little sister.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: Look, Andy, I know we have kind of a history...
Yeah, we had a history all right... The way Genghis Khan had a history with Central Asia.

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: But I seriously need your help right now! It's really important, and you're the only one I can trust!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Let me guess. Your fella's been giving you the funny business, and you want me to tail him and make sure he's not seeing some floozy on the side?

nodes.speaker: Paula
nodes.text: No, jerk! Something's been stolen, and I need you to track it down!
I had half a mind to tell her off right there...
